clue.text: A spinner giving help to snooker player

definitions.meaning: an arachnid that spins a web
a rest with raised legs that lifts the cue over a ball

explanation.surface: Someone who spins a ball is offering assistance to a snooker player.
explanation.definitionFit: The web-spinning arachnid shares its name with the long-legged cue rest in snooker.

clue.text: It may get an audience away from the central display

definitions.text: It may get an audience away from the central display

parts.words: It may get an audience away from the central display
parts.note: a minor attraction off to one side of the main event draws its own crowd

explanation.surface: Something draws spectators away from the main attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor entertainment at a fair or circus sits beside the main show and pulls in its own spectators.

clue.text: Unsuitable little devil takes cable to monarch

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
a cable is a thick rope
R stands for rex or regina, a monarch

explanation.surface: A little demon carries a cable to the king, which is not appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'to' simply join the pieces. The wordplay and 'Unsuitable' both point to IMPROPER; the grid's V for P in sixth place is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improper is inappropriate or unfitting for the occasion.

clue.text: One who makes sheep's eyes at royal water-carrier

definitions.meaning: a punning agent noun: someone who makes eyes like a female sheep
a large jug carried at royal banquets for hand-washing

explanation.surface: Someone gazes adoringly at a royal servant who fetches water.
explanation.walkthrough: Making 'sheep's eyes' means gazing lovingly; the first reading turns a female sheep into a verb with an agent ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-mouthed pitcher holds water for washing, so it carries water.

clue.text: Order scale trim for seafood

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters of scale are set in a new arrangement

parts.note: to lop is to trim or cut back

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange and trim fish scales before cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges SCALE into ESCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop-type shellfish, a bivalve eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Red Biddy responsible for her blushes? (or lack of them?)

definitions.text: Red Biddy responsible for her blushes? (or lack of them?)

parts.words: Red Biddy responsible for her blushes? (or lack of them?)
parts.note: red biddy is cheap red wine, but read as a red-coloured old woman of loose morals who might blush, or be shameless

explanation.surface: Cheap red wine makes a woman flush, or perhaps leaves her shameless.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Biddy is a British slang name for cheap red wine; here it is taken as a red woman called Biddy.
explanation.definitionFit: A promiscuous woman is called this, after the colour of sin, and she may be past blushing.

clue.text: Tawdry territorial decoration has gone all twisted

indicators.note: the decoration has gone means its letters leave the word tawdry

parts.note: TD is the Territorial Decoration, a British army reserve award

explanation.surface: A cheap regimental medal has become bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Decoration was a long-service medal for Britain's volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is out of line, turned or bent from its proper position.

clue.text: This flow of information isn't secret any more

definitions.text: This flow of information isn't secret any more

parts.words: This flow of information isn't secret any more
parts.note: liquid escaping through a hole and confidential news getting out share one verb

explanation.surface: News has escaped and is no longer confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: Information disclosed without authorisation has escaped like liquid through a crack.

clue.text: Goldsmith's work: reshape pottery when centre's scrapped

indicators.note: reshape tells us to remould the remaining letters into a new form
the middle letter of pottery, its fourth, is thrown away

explanation.surface: A goldsmith remodels a pot after its middle is discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the central T leaves POTERY, which 'reshape' rearranges. Oliver Goldsmith was an Irish poet and playwright, not a metalworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith wrote verse such as The Deserted Village, so his output is verse.

clue.text: Double portion of pudding sent back by Roman statute

indicators.note: sent back means the pudding word is read from right to left

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a cut-down portion of the word
lex is the Latin word for a law

explanation.surface: A double helping of dessert is returned under some Roman law.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-storey flat or a two-unit house is a double dwelling; in electronics it means two-way.

clue.text: Just remuneration for 1 down attendant

definitions.meaning: pay that is reasonable and equitable
the pay given to someone working at a funfair sideshow

explanation.surface: Fair pay for someone who works on a sideshow.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is SIDESHOW, a booth at a funfair, so its attendant earns pay at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable pay is reasonable reward for labour; a fairground worker earns pay at the fair.

clue.text: Hang back when it comes to doing some tango steps!

definitions.meaning: to delay or be reluctant to act
in the tango, the feet are slid along the floor

explanation.surface: Hesitating when it is time to dance the tango.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawdling reluctantly is the idiom; tango dancers literally slide their soles along the floor.

clue.text: Inform on the workroom

definitions.meaning: to betray someone to the police
a workshop, as in a machine ...

explanation.surface: Snitching on colleagues in the workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass on someone is slang for betraying them; a workshop is a place where things are made.

clue.text: Brother in reduced circumstances, poor fish!

parts.note: ill means poor or bad, as in ill health

explanation.surface: A monk who has fallen on hard times is pitied as a poor fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor fish' sounds like an unlucky person; 'fish' alone is the definition, and 'in reduced circumstances' paints the hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish related to the turbot, caught in European waters.

clue.text: Mean approach

explanation.surface: A two-word note: unkind, and getting closer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy people are called close; to draw close is to approach.

clue.text: Nero's fiddled an unconscious noise!

indicators.note: fiddled means tampered with, so the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: Nero played the fiddle and made a noise while out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned; here 'fiddled' rearranges NEROS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper's loud breathing is a sound made while not awake.

clue.text: Like a Tussaud celebrity getting wed without a kiss

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so wed goes round the other pieces

parts.note: X is the conventional sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: A waxwork star marries but gets no kiss at the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: WED wraps A and X. Madame Tussauds is a London museum of wax figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures in that museum are modelled in wax, so a celebrity there is made of it.

clue.text: The case of the diner who stayed to breakfast?

definitions.text: The case of the diner who stayed to breakfast?

parts.words: The case of the diner who stayed to breakfast?
parts.note: case means luggage, not a mystery: what a dinner guest staying the night brings

explanation.surface: Sounds like a detective story about a dinner guest who never left.
explanation.definitionFit: A small holdall for one night's stay carries what a guest needs until morning.

clue.text: When all has gone under, new brief is Heaven-sent, by Jove!

indicators.note: in a down clue, the second piece goes under, after, the first
new means the letters of brief are made into a fresh word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once everything has collapsed, a fresh legal brief is an answer to prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BRIEF to FIREB. Jove (Jupiter) hurled thunderbolts from heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazing meteor or lightning bolt falls from the sky, a weapon associated with the king of gods.

clue.text: Where ladybirds mass-produce the brinjal?

definitions.meaning: a factory where female birds lay ova in bulk

explanation.surface: Asking where ladybirds breed on the aubergine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladybirds' is lady birds, hens, not the beetles; a factory is a plant. Brinjal is the South Asian word for aubergine.
explanation.definitionFit: The American name for the aubergine, from the egg-shaped white fruit of early varieties.

clue.text: A flamboyant start to the pianist's recital?

definitions.text: A flamboyant start to the pianist's recital?

parts.words: A flamboyant start to the pianist's recital?
parts.note: a showy launch, or lifting the lid of the big concert piano

explanation.surface: A showy opening flourish at a piano recital.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish inauguration of a shop or event, and literally the lid of a concert piano being raised.

clue.text: Beast the Terriers rounded up becoming a mascot

indicators.note: rounded means the Terriers have gone round the beast
up in a down clue means the Terriers' letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: the Terriers is a nickname for the Territorial Army, TA
a mule is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A soldiers' animal mascot is rounded up by the regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TA to AT, and 'rounded' puts MULE inside it. The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm worn to bring luck or ward off harm serves as a talisman.

clue.text: Wound a burnt cloth round Eastern temples

indicators.note: wound, as in wrapped or coiled, signals the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A scorched cloth is wrapped around the head in an Eastern temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind; 'temples' are the sides of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A long scarf wound round the head is headgear worn by Sikh and other Asian men.

clue.text: Dumas detailed her development

indicators.note: development means the remaining letters evolve into a new order
detailed means de-tailed, losing the last letter

explanation.surface: Alexandre Dumas wrote in detail about a heroine's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts the S from DUMAS; 'development' rearranges DUMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, heroine of Tennyson's poem, so a female referred to as a pronoun.

clue.text: Religion is a hit

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or strike

explanation.surface: A faith that is a big success.
explanation.definitionFit: The monotheistic faith of Muslims, founded by the prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: He has a poor start making a pile

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man who begins badly ends up making a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a pile' reads as getting rich; 'a pile' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of things stacked untidily is a stack.

clue.text: Broke the chest

definitions.meaning: a woman's bosom, or a sculpture of the head and shoulders

explanation.surface: Penniless, with only a box left.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bankrupt is going bust; the bosom is a person's upper torso.

clue.text: Got up a get-up fit for Caesar

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word got is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Dressed in an outfit suitable for a Roman emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GOT to TOG.
explanation.definitionFit: The draped woollen robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome was formal costume.

clue.text: Left Queen to do the dirty work!

parts.note: Labour is the left-wing party in British politics
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen leaves the menial chores to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb but is the political left, Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual worker does heavy unskilled toil, the grimy jobs.

clue.text: Nothing found in sly Satan's work for busy fingers?

indicators.note: found in means the nothing is placed inside the other letters
sly suggests cunning trickery, so the letters of Satan's are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: The Devil gets work for idle hands, a twist on the proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sly' rearranges SATAN to SNATA, and 'found in' puts O after the S. The surface reworks the proverb that the devil finds work for idle hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical composition for piano or another instrument keeps a player's hands active.

clue.text: The little drinks Nanny serves

parts.note: small shots of spirits, or the toddlers a nursemaid looks after

explanation.surface: Grandma pours small measures of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A tot is a small measure of spirits and also a small child; Nanny can be a nursemaid or a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children are called tots; tiny tots also suggests small drams of whisky.

clue.text: A lot drawing first big parcel out

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of big

parts.note: to allot is to share out or distribute

explanation.surface: A big parcel goes out first, chosen by drawing lots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parcel out' reads as a noun phrase but is a verb meaning share.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret vote, originally by drawing coloured balls, decides by lot.
